title: Rate rises are back on the table as oil, France and AI rattle markets
dek: US inflation picked up again in September, French 10-year yields topped 5% for the first time since 2002, and an AI-driven selloff hit Asian chip markets.

mood.label: Nervous
mood.explanation: The VIX — the options market's gauge of expected S&P 500 swings — sat at 19.52 on Monday, up 5.86% on the week and 21.47% on the month, while CNN's Fear & Greed index stuck at 21, or 'extreme fear', against 37 a month ago. Reddit chatter has swung towards index trackers and speculative AI-adjacent names at once, which fits a market that is hedging and gambling in the same breath.

regions.headline: Inflation back at 4% as the Fed meets this week
regions.summary: September CPI rose to 4.02% a year, from 3.71% in August, with core at 2.79% and unemployment at 4.2%. Nearly all economists polled by Reuters expect the Fed to hold this week and raise rates in December. The 30-year mortgage averaged 7.32% on 22 October and home sellers are cutting asking prices.

regions.headline: French borrowing costs top 5% as politics bites
regions.summary: France's 10-year yield passed 5% for the first time since 2002 amid protests and a budget standoff, though Moody's held off a downgrade on Friday. Euro area inflation rose to 3.75% in September while the ECB's deposit rate stayed at 2.5%, with economists pointing to a December increase.

regions.headline: China grows 4.5%; chip-heavy markets sell off hard
regions.summary: China's economy grew 4.5% in the third quarter, helped by exports, and lending rates were left unchanged for a 17th month. Equity markets fell sharply: the Nikkei lost 4.2% on the week, the Hang Seng 4.0% and the KOSPI 5.2% as AI and chip jitters spread. The Bank of Japan meets on 29-30 October.

watchNextWeek: US Federal Reserve rate decision, Wednesday
Bank of Japan policy meeting, 29-30 October
European Central Bank rate decision, Thursday
China's Fifth Plenum of the Communist Party leadership
Brazil's presidential runoff result and Bulgaria's presidential runoff
body:
## Opening

This was a week in which the direction of travel on interest rates flipped in several places at once. American inflation is running at 4% again, euro area inflation is back near 3.75%, Indian rate-setters are debating how much more to tighten, and Japan's central bank is widely expected to keep nudging rates up. Meanwhile oil touched a five-month high on attacks on Saudi energy sites, France's borrowing costs crossed a line not seen since 2002, and a wobble in AI and chip shares knocked Asian markets. The S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,623.68, down 0.47% on the week; the Nasdaq fell 0.71%; the Nikkei dropped 4.2% and the KOSPI 5.18%.

## United States

The Fed meets on Wednesday with an awkward set of numbers. September CPI inflation came in at 4.02% year on year, up from 3.71% in August, while core CPI — which strips out food and energy — was steadier at 2.79%. Unemployment edged up to 4.2% in September from 4.1%. Nearly all economists in a Reuters poll expect the Fed to [skip October and raise rates again in December](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitAFBVV95cUxOZUFYOUZFZXZ4UWJSN1J6RkRxM1lkdGJsUFZRZ2puQkFnRk9rczVQZF9iUS12amVsUl9ESnA4MmNlUmFuVnBVY3BoeVZoVWx1dmwtSWdCa2tGUUlXeXdWR0o0U2o5NHdUend5d2o3c1NoUlZTQUNyWFFEalBHY25QMVptcnFoRnZiSk1JVDFyb1VFYkg0NGRJaXhWemlUY3gxX3YxeVh0YkNMSHNQU21pWkc0OVQ?oc=5), though [at least one large bank stuck with an October move](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuAFBVV95cUxPSkRFQlRfUm5NMFdrUTg1cHZSVFdfYUN4NG1qSUdpaFZkWlVGUkhGTkl3cGItUGVTUWtxVWZkRUV5RDdYeGY0SmVwLXctYjNKUi00bWR3NVV0dUdWNFQ3MUJSdW5ab19uZlZZODM0MWx5U0taMjJMX051N3dXRm90Mjd4eTlPRGhyYjdhaHBnRThoLTROaG42VW80cEFORUVPYV9zektiSjBFQi13bkxBZlF4WlMtdmxE?oc=5) even as markets bet against it. One analysis this week argued US inflation is [neither getting much worse nor much better, while consumers hold up](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMibkFVX3lxTE5qN0xzTlFoQTBld3pORlF4RW5NVVgzdmxXR3NadW1NZUpHckN4WURXTHZuc2dUZ0s0RVRaWUtQa1haZ0VsN0gyWW9SYk80aXVNUlk4UHpPUXVmc2l1UHV1aFVoaVhiRXBJaER5RHJR?oc=5).

Bond yields eased into the weekend: the 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.99% on Friday, with the gap between 10-year and 2-year yields (the "yield curve", a rough read on growth expectations) at 0.31 percentage points. That still leaves households paying a lot: the average 30-year fixed mortgage was 7.32% on 22 October. Estate agents report that [sellers are cutting prices and helping buyers close deals in a stagnant market](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxQOTNTNTg5NlBaRGZXQ1RtUjltdlpvYkFjMmxBRkZTLWhZVnVZSUFvM3pjTE9PQzE0MGRLbW9zODlwQ00zbWlkb1VObTRPQ2hPa1d2WWtaTVk0QXBhZVJabTVreEI2VW5oYW1ObjVCVmJaMW9lUGN4aXY3Z0tDWl9zVURsS0Frcl9TWTF6ZmhGejBBU2paU2NWSzRPSE9vSjFLY19qYTRSeV9VNlc0Mzk4?oc=5). Politics is pressing in too, with the midterms two weeks away: a Reuters/Ipsos poll put [President Trump's approval at a record low 31%](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuAFBVV95cUxOT2FjX0hUODU4WlBWVWtBbDJwVTBPdHVBTFpGTEpTcDhUYjQyaEZ2aE1RQkE1YjZlREp5ZkRFMXU2czFFVFFaQWQ2NmlJNzJVNGtQM0R0YW5fWDZ1Xzh3b0FBWHBfWVA5UFkwRUFic0FMQWJRTnRmY2xuU3N2dXZFai1ydGtVTC13QjdVM2txNTIyN1UzaGhPMFA4OG80dl8xbHFsUE90bmViTkdtSVNtRFhWakZkWWtH?oc=5), and a tariff pause on beef [angered some US ranchers while lifting Brazilian imports](https://news.google.?oc=5).

## Euro area

France was the story. The 10-year French government bond yield [passed 5% for the first time since 2002](https://news.google.?oc=5) as a budget deadlock and street protests collided; the government [deployed troops after weekend unrest and admitted failures](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxQQmJ1TFFHTzZnd2dhQWFDZ053eUx6SnN2NmdSSEZrR3FKLTMtMWpNem1TU0E2VUpRMGNuUl9NRXZ6X25haHNrMzlVMmd1MGQ4UFdyZFNyYWZQRjREWHNTdWQ0ZDktZjlqZFU1WWl5NF83OGwwVk01R19XZ3IzQlVXSWkxaVR6cVpfWWpWb01CbDJDbFNHUHNYUGdXcmk0d3pTeFEw?oc=5), and protest groups are [demanding more rallies](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuAFBVV95cUxNQmJMN1JUSWphZktVT1hXNmhHdXJYblhCMjFhREdZTzR2ZWhKdWgwRnB1enEwWFp3TWxJY2hvN0tQX0RpSXBFdFJVRUJiYzBvMWJiMTRrUWs4U0tRdE1YQ0xSdmZabkFGWTNROWZLQjBrc1l1LURSU2d1NG1aMXRVTmpHRXpUTHFYR0hzU3VEem9tX3JPWExBZXRidV83VmZYY2g3cTBZX0tkb2pzb3hZVUt0dnhWalN1?oc=5). On Friday, France [avoided a downgrade from Moody's](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihAFBVV95cUxPY2xNbGJrYUd0RHNhYS1kTFI5UGVfWG9UcDBLaHl1Y3lFT2xMZGVsb3gyVk5Td1lhVjJ3STRBM1RpQWl3NTlDTjJlb1hhTWNpZVJodzdfZUlHOTNHUjN4YkFOTmtRM1hDNjV6aVZHSmxtOVFzTWJ1QXBOREplMmNZZEJ3WVA?oc=5), a modest relief after a week in which [Paris-listed stocks, bonds and the euro all fell](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuAFBVV95cUxNby13cE9Lek5LUWdWSzdBVERHN1dDQmIyTXBjX1A5ZWlHaXdONzNUUjMxZUdxY0t3T3lOeVAwMnYyWG44RG9Gb0lrRGt5ZERFSkhLVkx6VHBIOFVzdGswWG9FTG9BeXdBMmpyUEEzSVhkRVJsWFk0UG1Rc3FLUGtvd19EOTV3ZVZTTU14QkxnSXlGZXZBQmg3cklHQTFHWHQybi0tZ3N5LU1CUmhVUkswX29xbE1UVGlO?oc=5). Why it matters beyond France: government borrowing costs set the floor for what banks charge companies, and a stressed sovereign tends to drag on credit conditions across the single currency area. Analysts were openly asking whether [French bond turmoil could force the ECB's hand](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiogFBVV95cUxPR1JMSXlmaWFKSGxIZFdTODdyQjhrTGRQTHFFa0xUdjEtOFpPeGVsSlJScVJKemRjNExUT3FDcFhDRDMtazJfRzF0QjV2d2NjQnZOMi0zR2g4WnJJd3lZdnlNRlRKTEE2aEh4LUMxRm0wRmJuXzkyanhFdWJUOVNCM19OWU5MbklDQnU3TFhGbkpZT1dYTkNWcXA4NTJ0QncyMWc?oc=5).

The ECB's deposit rate was 2.5% as of Thursday, with euro area inflation at 3.75% in September (up from 3.23%) and unemployment steady at 6.4% in August. The Financial Times reported the ECB is [on course for another rate rise this year](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMicEFVX3lxTE1NZGlXYVA2anNNdy03NTRIX2FPOG56T29UaDNua3dycmhKdnhzUXN3b29Nc294Y1ZSOFVscVRTMG9MOV9pRkVvTlljNGpjYTZlWFltS0VEQXRrY0VCNW43blpGM3FXUnFaLWxTdHFhZHQ?oc=5), and economists surveyed by Bloomberg expect [a December increase after a pause](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxOcEhTajNPZ3RPUmVuRTFxYjRmT08zWVZURDNQRHV0WF9xTXF4bHpqSXVhdjRiWkFJZFd1V2Q3djlLMndaWWZMaDZHWWJHalI5VS1Ka1Z4cUxkMTF3akRrZWVvY3NsdzEyU2xpYjhrYXpLSVY3Qm5mTGlMZDRzZnFWX3ctWEdDSDhJUG9LbUozMGVGREI1a1ZKcDJCRVg1WDNkXzhQeGpzeDdBWFZQNG5yWElB?oc=5). Euro area government debt was 88.8% of GDP in the second quarter. The Euro Stoxx 50 fell 0.85% on the week; the DAX rose 0.27%; EUR/USD was 1.12. In Britain, attention turns to the Budget, with the BBC framing the task as [sustaining a stronger economy through gathering clouds](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiW0FVX3lxTFBrRHZFaDg5djk1ZEpucUxXbmpGVnNremstS0owSTBYQlZUZkxXay0yR1htdkFULUJpYTJvTnNhU1RIOE04ek9sVzJCMk16cEQ4YXJKOVRJLXhfOUU?oc=5).

## Asia

China's third-quarter GDP grew [4.5% year on year, beating forecasts on an export surge](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiekFVX3lxTE8wdlh4YnA1SVpIR09PRFJnQWhwY2plT1JtWmEyRDZRaDM3MGlWdExQeTkyLWtITVBGeGhqMGFoREt1eG1zZkxhdGc3a2pualFsVlRMX1pXbHg1dlFiWEtXbmJhYlhsaXh2SDFOSlBaa3dvNVJiVExwQjRn?oc=5), with [September activity stabilising](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimAFBVV95cUxQalIzRWhyRDhhWkJPOERhaXJIMWQ5LUdIRWl5MGVkQmI3a3BsaVI4ZEE4UTBqaFEya2VpTGxZN0xIbXhFMmxXMkZzSURSeXlraFVtdGJxbFpUZFBvb1N2ZDVGVHBSM1VKcTRyZmpFenZkMnFDMGI4bUVmcjJDSHczZWRwUHB4akZjMjFvVXNKb2tERzgzNzRERg?oc=5) and growth [helped by an AI-related export boom](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxObjdWVVIyRU9UZ0V3aG1MMnRLM1hzQXRWZFZQeUxqbm1Ea0dhbUh5bVZrLWotbWZVOFlDVnZhRXRZY3dZQVkyR2JIZnlDaUxUcTJWaGpTbzhjanoyOXRIR1QxNE1udnY1ZnhNYUMzRDB0LUM2NDdRQ2dmSF9BcFZMS0cxYWhMa3p1RmxrMFlXYkZ3LVEwZGhrN0hKNGt1OEpweHVKdU8zb3pndjE4d1ItZjVsbXhoUEk?oc=5). Benchmark lending rates were [left unchanged for a 17th straight month](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxOVFZXT1FPSXBnXzZuWHVlNXhzVjNibHZCMV9GdGFSQUhGbDJoQTN2bDBFV3JzSnhjd1RjS3JlWGxjMkdINkx6S1E1ZlpBQkxqT3ZZRHQtUS1VT25HYWZUUDhnSVR3cXRUVGVmd3k5VVhRekJJazh6bVIyYUN5YllqcTV2eWFnWUZHRXJZMA?oc=5). Party leaders gather this week for the Fifth Plenum, with [Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign in the spotlight](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinAFBVV95cUxNeDRFc3AxTEo4WkdsTmE5RzVMcEhkOWlsUGoxVDJBVlNCaVJIeWRSN0tjMDdHOVV1MVlGLUhJX3ViNFhjYnZQQVlveUM3S1ZleFBWWkpJRTdtUjJNZ2hmR0h4NHhKN21vbVN0VjluV2JSUkNCcHgwNHN3aVdtTXcyMXFSd1VwNThlTHVRMnF0SUF1bGNYUHRZM0V3ZHQ?oc=5).

Japan's central bank meets on 29-30 October. It is expected to [hold rates around 1.25% while assessing whether underlying inflation has hit 2%](https://news.google.?oc=5), possibly [raising its inflation forecast](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivwFBVV95cUxNNEt0OVZkdE8tYkUwUDFsdDhhSDV5UURBdVNxVU5JdldQdFl0WkFpdzE4RkhhSUgxZG9LeVB4ZmxnZV9qWlFjNGctenU2T05DZWxlNVNGX3YteEM3TFg3Y2FUN3pJUVNjdF8zSFo4Rm13NGZjWXdUQ0RRZXNpbXpXYVI4UnUxc3F2SkV1OVRFMUpmcWlpN292VjBsM0hCeGFnSGdDaWpBZjg5V2l5TzRWbEhWQjM0eU9sRkpRM2ZCRQ?oc=5), with a Reuters poll pointing to a [hike to 1.50% in December](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqwFBVV95cUxQM01keWQ2YlhOUEZEODRRcFlSQzBtYnREaldoaTh0ZkpYVTFtYVJrbURVMDVyaEFkSFFoU2hiRmtfYVlYLW83SHdVMHlNbW9aV19oR3I1OG5ERnAwOV9EdjU0NDRkRUxVSXg3R2hJZUpiTXdIeWVSNVlfc1U0bGRndHhFNlhtbXA4N2I4dUhabFRsZDFsRUZFNWNHTDc0cWJPTGJnbU01aTR5VjA?oc=5). The yen was 157.37 to the dollar, having [strengthened during the week as risk aversion rose](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwgFBVV95cUxNbld3YU1Xa01GaW5wbDBIRjlJelhGMG9JaDhYM05JUmUtckZWaFZkMWVHZjBwaEw0MFBCZEtzWXVEelZXcVRPXzdvM2EzZXpvYllSNnlYR3JlV1lFUkZWMHNYcmpUU0l4SXRQVGY5ZjNWckdTdHpfcVRhT052SUdmSHBadEJRbmxIUmd0SHJHNWxuQjBxUGNwLTI0MHhoQmRWcENWbkE1dWNwaGpOYjY3NGEyZjIzeFBwbGJjem53TGp1UQ?oc=5). Japanese firms are also [compensating users as cyberattacks buffet the economy](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiswFBVV95cUxOalROR3UtSUJWekNjMEJyV1lUVHZqZ19BaU44dFQ3cEE2NnBHQXBEMmE0NVgyaDZtYlhqZk5ULXZvYUl5eVFaZUQ3T0t1eFdYYUZPQXJhM3Brby1xZGJic1Y4bFJ6YmIwVnNXS1ZoLWlvS0N2S1NUUHFadVJKLTJSZk9lZFF4bDBzdTMteVdKb281dHpOMHZuMTk1T2Q0eXhjcUM1ODJPUnVqR1NnQkJJSy1wdw?oc=5).

In India, the central bank governor said [rate cuts are off the table for now](https://news.google.?oc=5) and that further hikes depend on inflation, with the Reserve Bank's minutes showing [rate-setters flagging more hikes but wary of an aggressive cycle](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxPUGdWZGNpS05rb3hUX0JEdUYzbUcyeHZ3N1diczRRTW9jM1RFb1ZGdDA5cjVWVEZuUE5GRkItTjVEZWxCbHlTZHRRMW1FeUoxT1pTUWEzZGJVX0hYbFl5RjNKWDdTNjJFOUt4UGV2dTh4MXo0WDVaa2FrcWdWVzRvSWZaX054YllzOG9ZVlI5OVFuMHZYaFpudkVyVFJNZE4yWlFlMF9QZHU3UTdUZnBtQXJ5ZVRxZU0?oc=5) and the governor describing growth as [resilient at 7.1% with inflation a red flag](https://news.google.?oc=5). Korea took the hardest hit: [chip losses after a US selloff](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxOclJwVF83NmhVandVdnlLYWpJTzduMElzdkVDMjdXSS1xLWN1a0R2S1VibUxOaHVfR3F2LS1WaGNIWU8xVHJqYU1hUlFTTVlrd240RTNJelByN1lNSzNuOUdNUlB4dVJBTUpvVjhZOUE2Ri1YbURnd01Dd1NxUnBEeVJ4UDA5ekJPUkNoMmMwbXdKd3R0aUJSZ25peDIyRzl1UFRzSjZjZ2FMSGEzOV9qVw?oc=5) and a [weak debut for a Korean AI-cloud company](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxOSE9IMkh1QUwxd1E4TTJRVnFTaWpWb19DQk9hdWNwLVdvUWRvSVdWUlE4VE4wSWhabHloWENZLUNwS1ozV1dJY3hhNHdYY0NBUnA3N0dSMHBIcUpzMk1pV3lFMExOYjFrcmZwc0w5XzlTVGlPYVVjaVEwZXVSZzJERmE2VGhDNUh0NVVsdm1sYXZONW5YWjRXTEZWcGdzbmltb2s3bExmN1BQSndhYklid20yS1RpNnM?oc=5) left the KOSPI down 5.18% on the week and 20.61% over a month.

## Debt and politics

Energy and geopolitics drove prices. The Houthis said they [attacked Saudi oil pumping stations and Riyadh airport](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMizAFBVV95cUxORlYwOVl3Z1hlOFdacWVmeXZVNnVhejFlWDVOR0toczJ2MWNjT1FMRWZjVU0xd1hGaGtzNU9VcGdYSnR1Z2NVQjFfRVpKallEcEVuTzNweldmeEdYOE05UXFOejl1ekR1ZjlxUlhHT1NLa3J0cmZYWUxhSEs2eXNGb2xNNUJycVNWci1ZVzZUOXBSNGc0bzRJNWVTTnVlWHhXRlBrLWRTOV9HbmlJTmVfZk95N0FIQnBLQTlTa3N3eFBaVDJMWGptVU1VN3A?oc=5); the airport [reopened even as further strikes were threatened](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilwFBVV95cUxOUW9UZ0JLbE5OTy1EYlY0RTdEVS1iZm81X241Nk5GRVFLYzhzbVdOR0drbHZZeU44M3JiV1RqaW1aWVNjdWZUQ1A4dFZKakp2UjFyd1hvdXFhLXBQY2VkT0V2ZmtQaGZ4dGYzZktvT01LTWZmNnJudFNRZXdUbk42WTk5a193ZngzMFU3eXJPeFdhNUplRmxN?oc=5). Brent [hit a five-month high](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwwFBVV95cUxOYzBEdGVKYmZ3VVpJajg0TW5DN2VHVEM2aDVTcFJKQVduMnVMTU5NbVcyMGxBanBHY3VvMzJQR1VrQWM4b0hLeG1YaTFWcldTeU9yTlBXc3FiR1FtcUp0SmxhRkJkWmpmZ2x6X3VGZHZEUDNLTE9LTFZNSlBWWjNJVGtaV3YwWkc4QVhxbHozYkx5THpZMVlYVDAtd0dqbUMyOUcyVk91NEYxaFFCZklRWWhjQm5qN2NvVHdWdnZIQVJSMk0?oc=5) and settled at its [highest since April on Friday](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMixAFBVV95cUxPR2dZUC10TmJYRUk2RmM5WWpxaUx2XzBPZ0ZTV3hIR3BkaGFvZ3B2T1hhd0xEcXZOWk5LdXhLLUF5QU9XdTRQdnRyTk9jcmVNMEZvZlZBRW8xcG1TVW1fTkY2UnFrcXlVWlUwbDhRYk9pcW1fdEdzMVNRR2ZhYVl2T0RZa09uZTktZGFWRVRWSEpGeFhYVXVPR09zNDVaTVdiNDdRRHg3VFNyZWNNWVBmdkxGMWFOa05yN2NBRnRVZjF3eF9i?oc=5), before slipping on Monday as traders weighed [US-Iran diplomacy and demand destruction](https://news.google.?oc=5). Brent stood at $109.94 and WTI at $101.05 on Monday, with WTI down 2.52% on the week but up 9.13% on the month — a direct input into transport costs and headline inflation everywhere. Gold fell 3.21% on the week to $4,026.70; bitcoin fell 4.41%.

The electoral calendar is crowded: [Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in Serbia](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiAFBVV95cUxQMEpNNTMtaGhtbExPZTI4ME1rVk5DRENnWlRJSUJuMTQxc2V6Z01xdzU0V0xyTU4zSXdHMVZqN0RMU1VLQ2NCcnpQYXRVZTBKaHhQRGJzaWNYUXBmQVk0Q1JmVHhoVjdmeGlUd1BqeF9lMG83ZGpPWGRQbzRJQ2U1UENXYUY0LXdp?oc=5), [Bulgaria's presidential race went to a runoff on record low turnout](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilgFBVV95cUxPSHFOVmVhV1VWZHFRaTdTc3dzbTg5azlRZXk2MU1QMlA1ek55dmdZaTFsNGlCTjlYYnJrNV82SVpMcEdESlhmR1ZVSjhzRU9ZNnVYSjExMXZtTjBrWjFEajNOeThmUkVmUk95Z254dDBlQlJyVjFJWU13N3R1RHpsS21BT1kxNFlRVmtTXy1GU251THNMd2c?oc=5), [Brazil's Lula and Bolsonaro voted in the deciding round](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilgFBVV95cUxNYlNlX3hMQnNCZ0R2aVZJd0dhUmhoRF9YSDNFMlFOV3A1dXJPSHYyMXpwZTJQamtVTWd5aUZDc002OC1ReExrRGdLZXF4NDlVQlFfbm5tTWx2SWZxNHpFUWNXWU0wcnpJdlI3bzJhZWNMYXQ4VmZrZlVlQ3VMNEJscUVMNFhfZ01HYTgteVBqTW9POExhSVE?oc=5), and [Israel holds an election](https://news.google.?oc=5) amid [continued operations in the West Bank](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinwFBVV95cUxOMmFVbFU1aUF5RktLU21EaTk5alRrTVpDS3dUcEswWXBfVFl1M0pPNDdIV0lMeXpSMWVSQjY3S0wxNW9ZMV9rV0VKaFM5T1VfMEpQY1l4UU9MVk9xZFg2WGJTaTlBSUdkS0pPVDllOEN0LXBNQkFTOGlhSmRPbV83bHd2dVYyUkF5TDYxRGpHTmtnaG5Tb2tzN3hvakgwNWc?oc=5).

## AI and technology

The AI trade is now a macro story. S&P Global [flagged potentially hidden AI-related debt at hyperscalers](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMi_?oc=5) as spending surges, and [leaked Anthropic filings showed large losses](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMie0FVX3lxTE5fTWd2NkxkQ3U5XzBnd1MwYWx4Qk5hN3dCenBUbDhVdG1MMVNnQlhxZmJyZkhTQjBtUmZJRGlDazZxd0poWHdyNlhfUlJYWTJfMC16SThVS2ZDZGdkY3lCbWdycVRjcEl4WTdsYlptNzRUbEMtRDVfWEpZUQ?oc=5). Elon Musk said [so-called "neoclouds" are "cooked"](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxOdEpWNklXOC11OFYyYk5Pbzd3aDAtMExoQ2NQVW9WMWdIa3VWRDBES0x4TWx0WTJyUFJiNTFOMXZWTm9vSDVRS2VxeGo2QmR2dWJLMlVORWJ3Q2diUFkyZG9lZzg4WnZjbkd3dXZwVi16X2RIb1pVcldBWjJLbFlCNUtsU0YzLUpXYUpHUQ?oc=5) and that SpaceX would not buy them. Governments are being pulled in, with the US and China [forming rival AI blocs that leave other countries torn](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMigwFBVV95cUxPakhwUzlHbnJOemg0S0x1WlNQSUZIaEtpZlNSd0JtZmszRlg2S3QtTzZla3o2WjdDdTlhUFk0M0UteG84UTA4TndIbUgycFJrTFhlTG4yRXQ2STNDOFBuWE10eDhfcVRuLTNJbWRTRkhMSDZzSXVrcGdCZmpkVG9jS3loUQ?oc=5), and one report warned AI spending fears could [swamp big tech's earnings](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMixgFBVV95cUxNeUctUHVGc3l6MFJxbjM1Rml3cWswblZ6WVVBRUdFRlZEaDk0VHNrVDAzeTB1SkFaX2IxU2NSeHVYQTJKYVp4YVJ2b1EyRDhpQ3dZVFpOcVJtQ0F0S1JoazFpLXRnbURNRGtOWU50V3g5OWVCTDdTSkJoNHU0SXBNUHFKeGhtV01qdkFnUUNLV1dqdzRQY3Q0VGR5YWoyMXBqMFpxV0NjUUVuLUJSdnk2NDJzQU5HNmZ5T3U2NkgyeGpJU3ViNlE?oc=5). For finance teams, the practical question is less about share prices than about power bills, data-centre contracts and the credit markets now funding this build-out.

## Company news and results

With [more than a third of S&P 500 companies about to report](https://news.google.?oc=5), two semiconductor-linked sets of numbers stood out. Lam Research reported September-quarter revenue of $8.22bn, up from $6.72bn in the June quarter, with GAAP diluted EPS of $2.19 against $1.81, and guided to $8.60bn plus or minus $400m for the December quarter (per its SEC filing). Western Digital reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $4.381bn, up 55% year on year, non-GAAP diluted EPS of $4.64 versus $1.78 a year earlier, raised its quarterly dividend 17% to $0.175 a share and guided to about $5.1bn of revenue next quarter (per its SEC filing).

Elsewhere, SpaceX filed quarterly results with the SEC on 20 October, and in pharma, Roche [targeted the emerging oncology market with a new lung-cancer drug](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqwFBVV95cUxNVTJRUzBFdks0bXc0UnRpYWNaZU9PUmpNN0YxZzhQbGJLNG5fQ0JiSDc5UGZRbXBmRGYxS0g0eWdpNThTLXZKWFZBS1lxTGhsSWZJaWg1bXZaSTZBR0JwZ1VFbmE4Qk9OeWxnWG9oQjlqeEV3UktwZEMtcE55QUhMNGxBdW1ISWNPUlZZQl9MUE12OW9ZU0ZGMHd5NElROG1vUERkdlFuc0pEN0U?oc=5) while AstraZeneca [readied a portfolio of targeted cancer therapies](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqAFBVV95cUxPWnhINGdPMFVCdVRsWVFvMno4MU15NmRWSWpBUlk5X3EwUzNMcjJvNjNtVGhZWk1LbEI0cHhwNFJmb3dnM21tN1RLdWFfeVY3UWRwRzZvYk1Nc0djdkd6eWhrZlBwc2swMUM5X1lCZUdKdW5Fa09VTGdna3YzNzZIYldNVGdMVEp0TjZFaXhuNDY2N3pFSF9tRW43VC1UQUV2dW54UzhkZGo?oc=5). A trial of a cancer vaccine [cut melanoma recurrence or death risk by 42%](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiugFBVV95cUxNQzhYUnpreXZ6a25POUE0VC0tMFIta1AyVE43Q0oxcmx3TnlzQTBBdFhuQ3paZGlPdUJodWU0T2M1Q0g3OURlemo5aFNLRklNTUdZTjNQeGFZUFBJbmlzUGY5N3FDTG9uWHZmcnRwbmNzMHBNRFNMMm1DUXJBNklHVlplczNwbi1GVGpyVTltdGR2VVQ4UHIxbkNsOVdKNWUtR3BJQWFZNVJlNHJaeWpkSDhnVlZKQnZiblE?oc=5).

## Market mood

Nervous. The VIX closed at 19.52, up 5.86% on the week. CNN's Fear & Greed index was 21 — "extreme fear" — unchanged on the week and down from 37 a month ago. High-yield credit spreads, the extra yield investors demand to lend to riskier companies, were 3.40 percentage points on 22 October, up from 3.27 the day before: a small widening, not a rupture. Reddit's most-mentioned tickers mixed broad index funds with speculative AI and cloud names, an unverified but telling sign that retail attention is split between hiding and chasing. Monday brought [stock futures climbing after the S&P 500's losing week](https://news.google.?oc=5) even as [Asian shares slipped and oil fell](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimAFBVV95cUxNOGVDbFMzWWNkWEw1NzNQRUJLek52UWF2ZUh1dDVXM2FHNXhYekVEOUpNejc5djNNX0hTWDZiLVpaWUNnaGZ6b29iMS0wNHM0M0Y1eG9MdC1yVUVpTV9QbDlieDVrS3NLemIzTFdPOHFRTG1JSEpzbEc5MFR2aUhRMmFpSGJaZDJRV1d6bW1hUlVJUDdUSkFkMg?oc=5).

## What to watch next week

Three central banks, one Chinese plenum and two elections, in a week when the inflation data has already made the arguments harder.
